updated_captions.fig_energy: Energy conservation and collision statistics of the production runs (N = 1000, η = 0.35, 18 τ NVE). (a) Total-energy deviation E(t) − E(0) for the four integrators of the charged system (20+/20−, l_B = 5 σ, Δt = 0.005 τ): the naive splitting drifts by +1.48 kT, literal collision Verlet (cv) by −0.19 kT, kdk-phys by +0.075 kT and the shipped cv-phys by +0.033 kT (2.3 × 10⁻⁵ of |E₀|; inset without naive). (b) cv-phys: kinetic and potential energy fluctuate in antiphase with a standard deviation of 4.0 kT each while their sum changes by 0.034 kT at most. (c) Instantaneous temperature of the cv-phys run, ⟨T⟩ = 0.9990 ± 0.0027 kT. (d) Cumulative hard-sphere collisions in the neutral and charged runs against the Enskog rate N Γ_E/2 with Γ_E = 14.24 per particle per τ; the neutral run exceeds Enskog by 0.6 % and the charged run by 0.5 % (inset).
updated_captions.fig_pairing: Bjerrum pairing in the charged production run (20+/20−, l_B = 5 σ, cv-phys, 721 frames). (a) Number of +/− contact pairs (r < 1.2 σ) per frame, mean 8.3 (range 2–15). (b) Fraction of ions in a contact pair (38 ± 11 %) and fraction with an opposite ion within l_B/2 = 2.5 σ (86 %); dashed and dotted lines are the random-ion baselines obtained from 100 random 20+20 subsets of the neutral run, 0.585 ± 0.006 (2.5 σ) and 0.080 ± 0.002 (1.2 σ; standard errors of the subset mean); the hard-core-only estimate 1 − (1 − V_shell/V)^20 = 0.567 for 2.5 σ is a consistent cross-check. (c) Fraction of ions in connected +/− clusters of size 1–6: 10 % sit in clusters of three or more, almost all linear chains. (d) Survival function of contact-episode lifetimes: median 0.35 τ, mean 0.52 τ, 90th percentile 1.18 τ, longest 2.48 τ (3.3 s of movie); the dotted curve is an exponential with the same mean.
updated_captions.fig_structure: Static structure. (a) Neutral–neutral pair distribution of the hard-sphere run (η = 0.35, 0.01 σ bins, 721 frames, minimum image): the contact value extrapolated from 1.0–1.1 σ is g(σ⁺) = 3.01, against the Carnahan–Starling value 3.00 and 3.02 implied by the collisional virial Z = 5.233. (b) Ion correlations in the charged run (0.05 σ bins, all 721 frames; error bars are Poisson): g₊₋ reaches 16.8 ± 0.4 in the contact bin (≈20 extrapolated to σ⁺); same-sign pairs are depleted at contact (g ≈ 0.5), recover the bulk value by ≈2 σ (the + − + chain distance; 0.98 ± 0.04 over 1.95–2.25 σ) and show a weak second depletion (g ≈ 0.84) at 2.3–2.75 σ; ion–neutral correlations follow the neutral fluid beyond the first shell, while in the contact bin g_ion–neutral = 2.57 against 2.75 for neutral pairs, a 6.5 % deficit corresponding to the contact sites occupied by counter-ion partners (0.15 per ion in that bin). (c) Potential of mean force w₊₋ = −ln[g₊₋/g_HS] compared with the bare Coulomb pair energy −l_B/r and the linearised Debye–Hückel screened potential (κσ = 1.30): the effective attraction at contact is −1.81 ± 0.02 kT, far weaker than the bare −5 kT, because the other 38 ions screen the pair; the DH curve is shown only as a scale since l_B/σ = 5 is outside its range of validity.
updated_captions.fig_dynamics: Single-particle dynamics (trajectories unwrapped through the periodic box). (a) Mean-squared displacement versus lag time for neutral spheres in the neutral run, neutral spheres in the charged run and the 40 ions, with t² (ballistic) and t (diffusive) guides and the Enskog prediction; the slopes over 1–4 τ give D = 0.123, 0.125 and 0.124 σ²/τ (1.17 × Enskog), i.e. ions and neutrals diffuse alike. (b) Distribution of the displacement per frame (Δt_frame = 0.025 τ): mean 0.038 σ for neutrals, 0.039 σ for ions, maximum 0.14 σ; the dashed curve is the Maxwell speed distribution times Δt_frame. (c) Free-flight check: fraction of neutral spheres whose displacement vector is identical over two consecutive frame intervals, 0.491 on average against exp(−2ΓΔt_frame) = 0.489 for the measured collision rate Γ = 14.32 τ⁻¹.
updated_captions.fig_order: Energy-error order test on the production system (N = 1000, η = 0.35, 20+/20−, l_B = 5 σ): maximum |E(t) − E(0)|/N over 2 τ of NVE dynamics versus the step h for the four integrators, with the fitted log–log slopes in the legends and dashed reference lines ∝ h and ∝ h². (a) Equilibrated start (15 τ with charges on): the shipped cv-phys is second order (slope 2.02) whereas the literal HLL collision Verlet is only sub-first-order (slope 0.73) and 35× less accurate at the production step h = 0.005 τ; kdk-phys gives 1.82 and the naive splitting 1.09. (b) Same test from the un-equilibrated start with Ewald (solid; slopes 1.40 / 0.78 / 1.69 / 0.89) and with the smooth DSF Coulomb model (dashed, cv-phys 1.92, cv 1.21). The Ewald real-space truncation erfc(αr_c) ≈ 7.5×10⁻⁵ gives an energy floor of ≈ 0.5–1 × 10⁻⁶ kT/N that limits the cv-phys curve at h = 0.0025 τ (local slope 1.0 between 0.005 and 0.0025 τ; 6 × 10⁻⁷ kT/N in (a)); cv and naive are flat there because of their own first-order collision error (65× and 229× above the floor, local slopes 0.11 and −0.06), and kdk-phys is not yet affected (local slope 2.9).
updated_captions.fig_pair_closeup: Close-ups of the charged production run in the x-ray style of the movie (neutrals 85 % transparent, ions opaque; red +, blue −), re-rendered at 3× the movie resolution for the three frames chosen from a cluster scan with the r < 1.2 σ contact criterion: (a) an isolated +/− contact pair at the front face of the box at t = 16.27 τ (nearest other ion 2.5 σ away, no other ion inside the circle in projection, no neutral in front of it), (b) a linear four-ion chain (+ − + −) at t = 9.75 τ and (c) a linear five-ion chain (− + − + −) at t = 9.22 τ, 42 σ from the camera. Dotted circles enclose the cluster; the bar gives 1 σ at the depth of the cluster. Such chains are transient: clusters of four or more ions exist in 142 of the 721 frames and the largest cluster seen has six ions.
updated_captions.fig_render_cost: Rendering cost per 1280×720 frame on the 4-core Xeon box (no GPU), measured on the 1000-sphere test trajectory including overlay and PNG writing: OVITO/Tachyon cpk at final quality (16 ambient-occlusion samples, 16 Tachyon threads) takes 1.43 s per frame, i.e. ≈ 17 min for a 721-frame movie, the x-ray preset 1.27 s (≈ 15 min), the AO-free draft preset 0.26 s (≈ 3 min) and the numpy fallback renderer with 4 worker processes 0.24 s wall (≈ 3 min). The annotated vertical ticks mark the three production movies: 1028 s and 1031 s wall for render plus encode of the two cpk movies (1.43 s per frame, two coinciding ticks) and 896 s for the x-ray movie (1.24 s per frame).
